arguments.summary: A pull request replaces constant-time password hash comparison (hmac.compare_digest) with standard string equality (==), introducing a timing attack vulnerability.

evidence.note: Standard equality operator (==) short-circuits on the first mismatch, leaking timing information about the hash value.
Previous code correctly used constant-time comparison via hmac.compare_digest.

findings.claim: Replacing hmac.compare_digest with a standard string equality comparison (==) introduces a timing attack vulnerability when verifying password hashes.
findings.explanation: Comparing password hashes using standard equality (`==`) allows an attacker to measure small differences in response time to determine correct bytes of the hash one by one (timing attack), weakening password hash verification. Constant-time comparison (`hmac.compare_digest`) must be used to prevent this.
